expect:
Arguments in support:
• Jesus taught that Christians should help the poor — he told a rich man to sell everything and give to the poor (Mark 10:21). This suggests giving to charity is a Christian duty.
• The Parable of the Sheep and Goats (Matthew 25) teaches that those who help those in need are serving God himself: “Whatever you did for one of the least of these, you did for me.”
• “Faith without action is dead” (James 2:26) — Christians must put their beliefs into practical action, and donating to charities like CAFOD, Tearfund, and Christian Aid is a direct way to do this.
• The causes of world poverty (debt, natural disasters, unfair trade) require collective action that individual Christians cannot address alone — charities provide the infrastructure to make a real difference.
Arguments against:
• Not all Christians can afford to donate money — they may be living in poverty themselves. They can still follow Jesus’ teachings through prayer, volunteering, or campaigning.
• Some Christians may argue that helping the local community is equally important — Jesus taught “love your neighbour” (Mark 12:31), which could mean those closest to you.
• Some may argue that evangelism and spreading the gospel is more important than financial giving — the Great Commission focuses on making disciples, not on charity work.
• There are concerns about whether donated money always reaches those in need due to corruption or inefficiency.
Conclusion: A justified conclusion should weigh both sides. Many Christians would agree that giving to charity is important but not the only way to fulfil their duty to help others.
Top band (10-12): Well-argued, well-justified arguments for and against, linked together, leading to a reasonable conclusion with reference to Christian teaching.
Upper-mid band (7-9): Good, well-justified arguments for and against, linked together.
Lower-mid band (4-6): Different arguments for and against with justification, or several linked justified arguments for one position.
Lower band (1-3): One argument with justification.
